answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The dune multiplier is published, charged in spiral, and ivory lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2152 identities would post 2150 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
